context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Balancing test: Whether the redactions strike a reasonable balance between Anthropic's legitimate interests and society's interest in transparency; and
paraphrase: The review will assess whether redactions reasonably balance Anthropic's interests against society's interest in transparency.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Materiality: Whether any of the redactions in the public report are material to any of the external reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report's claims.
paraphrase: The review will assess whether redactions materially affect the reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report.

excerpt: Public comments. We will ask the external reviewer to memorialize its findings on the topics above in a written report that is made public.
paraphrase: External reviewers will be asked to produce a public written report memorializing their findings.

excerpt: External reviewers will be bound by obligations not to disclose confidential information (e.g., confidential intellectual property, matters of national security, or proprietary details such as model architecture, cost, or size), but beyond that will not be restricted in what they can publish, including concerns about the Risk Report or Anthropic's conduct in connection with the external review.
paraphrase: Reviewers must keep confidential information private but otherwise face no restriction on publishing concerns, including about Anthropic's conduct.

excerpt: For example, we may redact information if sharing it would endanger our legal right to treat it as confidential. This would be an uncommon situation.
paraphrase: The footnote gives an example: redacting information to preserve a legal right to confidentiality, noted as uncommon.

excerpt: It does not mean we would redact information merely because it is sensitive or to reduce the risk of a leak.
paraphrase: Sensitivity alone or leak-risk reduction alone is not sufficient justification for redaction under this footnote.

excerpt: We commit to the following governance measures to promote internal and external accountability.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to governance measures for internal and external accountability.

excerpt: Responsible Scaling Officer: We will maintain the position of RSO, a designated member of staff who is responsible for the implementation of this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain an RSO position responsible for implementing the policy.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (1) as needed, proposing updates to this policy; (2) approving relevant model development or deployment decisions based on our risk assessments; (3) reviewing major contracts (e.g., deployment partnerships) for consistency with this policy;
paraphrase: The RSO's duties include proposing policy updates, approving development/deployment decisions, and reviewing major contracts for policy consistency.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (4) overseeing the implementation of this policy, including the allocation of sufficient resources; (5) receiving and addressing reports of potential instances of noncompliance; and (6) making judgment calls on policy interpretation and application.
paraphrase: The RSO's duties also include overseeing implementation and resource allocation, addressing noncompliance reports, and making interpretive judgment calls.

excerpt: Internal transparency: We will share final, unredacted Risk Reports with Anthropic's regular-clearance staff.
paraphrase: Anthropic will share complete, unredacted Risk Reports with regular-clearance staff.

excerpt: Noncompliance reporting: We will maintain a process for Anthropic staff to submit anonymous or identified reports regarding potential noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a process for staff to report noncompliance, anonymously or identified.

excerpt: Staff will have more than one option for who receives these reports, including the RSO, and at least one executive who does not report to the RSO.
paraphrase: Staff can choose among multiple report recipients, including the RSO and an executive independent of the RSO.

excerpt: When we receive a report, we will promptly investigate, take appropriate and proportional corrective action if it is substantiated, and document the report and our findings.
paraphrase: Upon receiving a report, Anthropic will investigate promptly, take proportional corrective action if substantiated, and document findings.

excerpt: We will provide quarterly updates to the Board regarding reports of potential noncompliance, whether substantiated or not.
paraphrase: Anthropic will give the Board quarterly updates on noncompliance reports regardless of substantiation.
